extracted.intended_audience: Scholars, institutions, and practitioners applying for NEH grants; prospective NEH panelists and program staff
extracted.subtask_description: Official NEH guidance describing the multi-level peer review and decision process for NEH grant applications, including panel composition, reviewer behavior, review criteria, ratings, staff synthesis, Council review, and final Chair decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanities significance
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH’s review criteria emphasize humanities significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether the proposed project addresses an important question or topic in the humanities; applicants should consult the specific program criteria for further detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant abilities and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH’s review criteria emphasize the applicant’s abilities and qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess the track record, expertise, and capacity of the people and organizations proposed to carry out the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH’s review criteria emphasize the proposal’s clarity of expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be clearly written so reviewers can understand aims, methods, and outcomes; clarity affects reviewers' ability to judge merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH’s review criteria emphasize the project’s feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider whether the project can reasonably be completed within the proposed timeframe and with the proposed resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project design
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH’s review criteria emphasize the project’s design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators evaluate the conceptual and methodological design of the project—how well thought-out and appropriate the approach is for the aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project cost
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH’s review criteria emphasize the project’s cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider whether the budget is reasonable and justified for the scope of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work plan
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH’s review criteria emphasize the project’s work plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear, realistic timeline and allocation of responsibilities are expected; reviewers judge whether the work plan supports successful completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of program-specific published review criteria and guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviews and ratings must be based on NEH's published review criteria and program guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since review criteria may vary by program, applicants should consult the criteria of the specific grant program to which they apply; reviewers are required to follow those published standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratings scale (E, VG, G, SM, NC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluators assign initial ratings chosen from: E for Excellent, VG for Very Good, G for Good, SM for Some Merit, and NC for Not Competitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators enter preliminary comments and initial ratings after early review. Ratings may be raised or lowered after panel discussion. Evaluators provide individual ratings—panels are not asked to reach consensus or to rank applications as a panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest recusal
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases of a conflict of interest, evaluators will recuse themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must identify and step aside from evaluation when conflicts exist; recusals affect panel assignments and deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panelist selection considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Program officers select evaluators for their expertise in relevant disciplines, topics, and areas, as well as overall breadth of knowledge in the humanities; other considerations may include institutional type, past panel experience, or other demographic characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH assembles panels to reflect relevant subject-matter expertise and a diversity of perspectives and institutional types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on panel service
rubrics_metrics.description: No evaluator may serve in consecutive years for the same grant program or on more than two convening panels in any calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels are reconstituted each competition and NEH does not have standing panels; this rule helps ensure rotation and broadened participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application eligibility check
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH program officers check applications for eligibility before assigning them to panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only eligible applications are forwarded to panels; eligibility is determined according to program rules and guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment to panels
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH program officers assign applications to panels based on academic discipline, institutional type, project area, or project type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment aims to match applications with evaluators who have appropriate subject-matter expertise or relevant contextual knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel size and evaluator count
rubrics_metrics.description: Program officers typically assign 15 to 40 applications to a panel and select three to five evaluators per panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This operational parameter shapes workloads and the number of independent evaluations each application receives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer access and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH provides evaluators with online access to the applications several weeks in advance of a panel meeting; at this stage evaluators read applications, enter preliminary comments, and assign initial ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure application materials are complete and clear well in advance of deadlines because reviewers will rely on submitted documents to form initial impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel discussion and rating revision
rubrics_metrics.description: In some programs, evaluators may meet virtually to discuss the applications, enter additional written comments, and assign their final ratings; informed by the panel discussion, they may raise or lower their initial ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program officers organize proceedings according to initial ratings, moving from highest- to lowest-rated applications; panel discussion can change individual evaluations but panels are not required to reach consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff synthesis and recommendation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH staff organizes panel results and, for highest-rated applications, summarizes reviewers' comments and recommends the most meritorious applications while maintaining an even level of quality among the recommended proposals across all panels in a grant program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff recommendations are based on reviewers' ratings/comments plus staff judgment about relative merit and programmatic balance across panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Council review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Council on the Humanities, an advisory body, meets (typically twice a year) to review staff recommendations; Council members discuss applications, vote on staff recommendations, and finalize recommendations to the Chair. By law, the Council is required to review applications for financial support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council deliberations occur over two days and are organized by committees; their recommendations are advisory to the Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair's final decision authority
rubrics_metrics.description: After Council deliberations, the NEH Chair takes into account the advice provided by the review process and, by law, makes all funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chair considers the totality of reviewer, staff, and Council advice before issuing final funding determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and confidentiality policies
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH seeks transparency while protecting confidentiality: it is public information that an evaluator served on an NEH panel (panels announced in the Federal Register; panelists listed in annual reports), but the public may not attend panel or Council meetings. NEH announces award winners but does not announce names of unfunded applicants. Applicants may request evaluators' ratings and written comments, though NEH does not provide the names of evaluators with their comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can obtain reviewers' comments and ratings on request; however, evaluator anonymity is preserved in normal circumstances. FOIA litigation could affect confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require use of Grants.gov application package and deadline submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants use guidelines and the Grants.gov package to prepare materials and must submit the application package to Grants.gov by the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following the specified application forms, attachments, and deadlines is a prerequisite for an application to be accepted and reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panelist recruitment and diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH recruits panelists from every state and draws on a wide and diverse pool of scholars and other humanities experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH invites scholars, teachers, administrative staff, and members of the public with humanities backgrounds to sign up for panel consideration; diversity in geography and expertise is an explicit recruitment goal.
